# Once v0.4.0

Changes since v0.3.0, grouped by platform.

## Upgrade notes

- **Linux and macOS desktop builds ship for the first time.** Linux gets a
  `.deb` and a portable ZIP, macOS a `.dmg` and ZIP for Apple Silicon and
  Intel. The macOS bundles are ad-hoc signed and not notarized: open the first
  launch via Control-click → Open. Neither platform updates itself yet; the
  version row offers **Check latest release** instead.
- **The "What? Wait, who, why?" AI add-on now comes bundled** and installs on
  first start. Remove it from Settings → Once Add-ons if you do not want it;
  the removal syncs and the add-on is not offered again. It makes no requests
  until you open its tray.
- Electron moves to Electron 45 (Chromium 155).

## Across all platforms

- **Once add-ons.** Add-ons extend Once itself: collectors, presenters, story
  trays and actions, declared in a manifest and, when scripted, run in a
  sandboxed frame with no network of its own. Install from a URL, a folder or
  a ZIP; a per-device code cache and a manual update check keep URL installs
  current. Add-ons get capabilities, storage, panel actions and options pages,
  and their sources fold behind a Sources heading in the settings.
- **AI assistant add-on.** The bundled "What? Wait, who, why?" add-on explains
  a title, summarizes the article and answers follow-up questions in a tray
  under the story, with Markdown, grouped citations that link every named
  source, and Tavily as a search fallback. A tray conversation can continue on
  a larger surface: an Electron tab, an extension page or the mobile reading
  view.
- **Stored story content.** Feed text and saved page articles are kept as
  story attachments, so the reader opens them offline on every platform;
  bookmarking and per-source triggers decide what is stored.
- **Reader read-aloud with an offline voice.** The reader reads articles with
  the system voices or the bundled Wafli SLT voice, which works without any
  platform speech engine. Loose paragraphs are read, footnote markers and long
  code blocks are skipped.
- **Find in page** on Electron (Ctrl+F in the content pane) and from the
  mobile browser sheet, in both browser and reader mode.
- **Story-source cache timing.** Each source has its own cache window,
  launches are cache-first, and the cache section has explicit controls.
- Story buttons are configurable per platform; global search results show
  stored read and star state; the keyboard cursor is a pill rather than a row
  fill; settings share one row shape and one switch; the Nitter collector is
  gone.

## Electron (desktop) and extensions (Firefox & Chrome)

- Settings navigation follows mouse back and forward, sources have an enable
  toggle and a ⋮ menu, and long back-button labels truncate instead of
  wrapping the title bar.
- Firefox add-ons run in a packaged local sandbox; the extension's
  conversation pages belong to the panel that opened them.

## Electron (desktop)

- **Firefox extensions in the embedded browser.** Once hosts Firefox-style
  WebExtensions in its own runtime: uBlock Origin and Violentmonkey ship
  bundled, and any Manifest V2 or V3 extension installs from a Mozilla
  Add-ons listing, a direct XPI link or a local file. The Add-ons site itself
  shows an **Add to Once** button. Manifest V3 extensions get
  `declarativeNetRequest`, `scripting` and `browser.action`. Filter lists and
  userscripts are synced settings that are handed to both bundled extensions.
- An **extensions panel** sits beside the address bar with direct actions and
  toolbar pinning; popups size from their own content.
- **Tabs and windows.** Closed-tab history survives a restart, the tabs a
  killed session had open lead the reopen stack, new tabs open right after
  the active one, list stories open in a foreground tab of their own, the tab
  speaker icon lights green while a tab is audibly playing, and the address
  bar menu gains Paste and Go.
- **Accessibility is opt-in.** The forced full accessibility tree cost seconds
  of main-process time per large page; a "Screen reader support" setting
  enables it, and Electron 45 ends the per-node event flood on resize.
- A manual **Check latest release** for installs without Squirrel updates.
- Credentials stay saveable when the OS refuses the `safeStorage` key: they
  are kept unencrypted in the profile with a warning and re-encrypted on the
  next successful save.
- Linked add-on folders reload on edit and show where they run from.

## Mobile (Android & iOS)

- **Android browsing runs on GeckoView** with uBlock Origin and Violentmonkey
  built in. Extensions install from AMO or a signed XPI with a native
  permission dialog, options and popup pages, and extension-created tabs;
  extension pages are framed under the app's own header. Navigation
  readiness, stalled loads, process loss and memory pressure recover with
  bounded retries.
- **Background media playback** for opted-in pages in the Android reading
  view, with notification and lock-screen controls and YouTube metadata; the
  reading menu handle drags to dismiss.
- Substory comments, story tag pages and `_self` links open in the reading
  view instead of the system browser; shared add-on trays show in Reading and
  respect Android shell insets.

## Build and tests

- Release workflow builds Linux and macOS Electron artifacts and verifies all
  four artifact sets before publishing.
- The bundled extension archives are fetched against pinned SHA-256 hashes;
  the bundled add-ons are inlined at build time.
- CI failures explain themselves instead of timing out; Firefox add-on runs
  scale their waits and capture failure evidence; the Electron smoke keeps
  app logs of passing tests.
- Calibrated controls catch native tab rendering regressions; the visual
  review harness was repaired; Electron test profiles use the mock keychain.
- Coverage for GeckoView navigation, fault recovery and memory pressure with
  Android instrumentation tests.
